summary: The first question is answered and closed, so this turn opens an independent lead on the other axis: a bounded randomized safety exploration of the captured snapshot. It adds a second test to the harness that runs three real raft state machines with in-memory storage for 300 steps per seed, with random connectivity masks that change per node, per-message drop decisions, random ticks, random member proposals, random campaigns and random leader transfer requests, then applies committed entries and checks five monitors after every step: one leader per term, applied entries immutable per node and index, the same entry for the same index across nodes, committed index monotonic per node, and every previously applied entry present in the log of a state machine that reports itself leader. Violations would be emitted as safety_violation events and each seed ends with a summary event. A local run in the scratch copy reports seed 11 with 92 proposals, 10 campaigns, 12 transfers, 358 messages delivered and 288 dropped, 24 applied indexes and zero violations, and seed 23 with 98 proposals, 3 campaigns, 14 transfers, 199 delivered, 160 dropped, 8 applied indexes and zero violations, so this is a bounded negative with an explicit scope rather than a finding: membership changes, snapshots and restarts are excluded and no absence claim is made beyond the explored seeds. The submission is an exploratory basis with no fixed requirement, as the harness instructions allow, and its retained receipt will be interpreted next.
